question: What source-authoritative transverse-shear/shear-area formulation does CAESAR II 14 use for isotropic metallic straight-pipe flexibility, and how should it compose with independently owned bend, B31J tee, and reducer mechanics?
constraints: No solver or profile mechanics change in I026.
No new numeric kappa or effective shear area may be selected by fitting BM4_NL reactions, displacements, source actions, node20090, node20250, node20390, or source44.
Vendor documentation and primary mechanics literature are admissible; secondary summaries are not authority for promotion.
A primary mechanics formula such as Cowper is not evidence that CAESAR implements that formula unless CAESAR applicability is independently established.
Absence from searched documentation is not proof that CAESAR omits transverse shear; unresolved implementation authority fails closed.
requiredAuthorityFields: whether isotropic metallic pipe includes transverse shear deformation in the static piping stiffness path
definition of shear modulus used for isotropic materials
effective shear area or shear-correction coefficient
dependence on section geometry and Poisson ratio
relationship, if any, to bend flexibility corrections
relationship, if any, to B31J tee rotational flexibility
relationship, if any, to condensed reducer internal beam mechanics
acceptanceRule: I026 may authorize a later numeric/formulation candidate only if the CAESAR-compatible metallic-pipe shear law is pinned to vendor or equivalent implementation authority with unambiguous applicability. Otherwise I026 closes as an accepted authority-boundary finding and no numeric candidate is authorized.
decisionReason: Collect and classify primary/vendor evidence without changing mechanics.
